How to calculate the price per 100g

The price per 100 grams calculator makes it easier to compare products sold in different package sizes. Instead of looking only at the total price, you can use the same 100 g reference for every product.

The formula is simple: divide the product price by its weight in grams and multiply the result by 100:

Price per 100g = (Price ÷ Weight in grams) × 100
Example: £3.20 ÷ 400g × 100 = £0.80 per 100g

Tips for comparing prices at the supermarket

  • Always compare the same unit: price per 100g for solids, price per 100ml for liquids.
  • Bigger is not always cheaper: larger packs usually cost less per 100g but not always — use this calculator to check.
  • Check own-brand vs branded: own-brand products often have a much lower price per 100g for similar quality.
  • Watch out for "special offers": multipack deals do not always work out cheaper per 100g than the standard pack.

Why use price per 100g?

Supermarkets in the UK are legally required to display the unit price (price per 100g or per kg) alongside the selling price for most food products. This makes it easier to compare value without doing mental arithmetic. This calculator automates that comparison for any product.

Frequently asked questions

How do you calculate the price per 100g?

Divide the product price by its weight in grams and multiply by 100. For example, a 500g product costing £4.00 has a price of £0.80 per 100g: (4.00 ÷ 500) × 100 = £0.80.

Can I enter the weight in kilograms?

Yes — select "Kilograms" from the unit dropdown and enter the weight in kg. The calculator converts it automatically to grams before calculating.

Does this work for liquids too?

Yes. Select millilitres or litres from the unit dropdown to calculate the price per 100ml instead. This is useful for comparing drinks, oils, sauces and other liquid products.

Why is the bigger pack sometimes more expensive per 100g?

It does happen — especially with premium or organic products where larger packs are sold at a premium. Promotional pricing can also distort the comparison. Always check the unit price rather than assuming bigger is better value.

Is price per gram the same as price per 100g?

No. Price per gram gives the cost of one gram, while price per 100g multiplies that by 100 for a more practical comparison. Most supermarket shelf labels show price per 100g or per kg rather than per gram.
